articles.title: Base App Is Coinbase Wallet Again: Will Traders Notice?
articles.summary: Coinbase restores the Coinbase Wallet name. The app now points traders at leverage, prediction markets and tokenized stocks.
articles.body:
Coinbase has restored the Coinbase Wallet name to the platform it renamed Base App in July 2025, ending a one-year attempt to turn a crypto wallet into a social network.

The app now points at leveraged bets, prediction markets and tokenized shares across more than 10 blockchain networks.

The rename closes a pivot that began much earlier. BeInCrypto reported the trading-first pivot in January, eight months before the branding caught up.

Base is Coinbase's own blockchain network, launched in 2023. The 2025 rename put that network's name on the consumer app, alongside a feed, messaging and mini apps.

Base creator Jesse Pollak handed the app back to Coinbase in July and called his on-chain social bet a failure.

Chief executive Brian Armstrong had already called time on creator coins. Those tokens let fans buy a stake in a post or a personality.

Most spiked on attention, then collapsed. BeInCrypto counted four Base experiments that flopped before Armstrong pulled the plug. They were:

"We messed up, time to turn the page," Armstrong said at the time.

Coinbase Wallet now routes users to Hyperliquid for perpetual futures. Those are contracts that let traders bet on price using borrowed money, with no expiry date.

It also carries prediction markets and tokenized stocks, which are shares tracked on a blockchain instead of at a broker. Robinhood Chain and Monad join the supported networks.

Robinhood Chain already ranks among the leading tokenized stock venues, according to Grayscale. Coinbase says the wallet will test products its main exchange cannot list first.

Perpetual futures remain closed to United States users, a limit Washington is now weighing for Hyperliquid.

Coinbase has not published a fee schedule for the wallet. It has also not said whether the trading push grew user numbers.

Coinbase web pages still showed Base App branding on Thursday, hours after the name was said to have changed. Traders who only swap tokens will notice a new icon and little else. Those reaching for leverage will notice the wall.

articles.title: Trump's White House Endorsement 'Extremely Positive,' Says Hyperion DeFi CEO: Executive Explains Why HYPE Ownership Is 'Beneficial'
articles.summary: Hyunsu Jung, CEO of Hyperion DeFi, Inc., stressed the company’s goal of steadily growing its Hyperliquid reserve, noting that greater HYPE ownership is benef...
articles.body:
Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

Hyunsu Jung , CEO of Hyperion DeFi, Inc. , stressed the company's goal of steadily growing its Hyperliquid reserve, noting that greater HYPE ownership is beneficial.

Hyperion DeFi holds a long-term strategic treasury of the native token of the Hyperliquid Layer-1 blockchain, specifically built for trading perpetual futures, spot assets and other financial derivatives.

It currently holds roughly 1.93 million HYPE, worth over $166 million, on its balance sheet, according to CoinGecko, making it the second-largest HYPE treasury company after Hyperliquid Strategies Inc. .

In an email interview with Benzinga, Jung said the company plans to "consistently accumulate" HYPE over time, funded by revenue from expanding business lines and "accretive purchases" through access to public markets.

"We believe that more HYPE ownership is beneficial, given the trend that future new primitives on Hyperliquid will require some quantity of HYPE stake," Jung added.

That said, Jung clarified that Hyperion DeFi is not solely focused on accumulating HYPE.

The company runs institutional-grade validators to generate native staking rewards through its HYPE holdings, while also allocating HYPE to core DeFi primitives such as lending, borrowing, and vault strategies.

Trump's Endorsement 'Extremely Positive'

The Hyperliquid ecosystem has kicked into high gear after President Donald Trump said at a White House summit that the administration is "working hard" to bring the decentralized exchange to the U.S. market "in a fully compliant and legal fashion."

The HYPD stock is up 37% in a month, while the HYPE token has surged 58%.

"It's extremely positive to see Hyperliquid acknowledged at that level, and to see support from key agencies like the CFTC clearing the way for Hyperliquid to be available in the U.S.," Jung said.

Hyperion DeFi raised its full-year 2026 adjusted gross profit guidance to $7 million-$8 million on Tuesday, up from $5 million-$7 million. The Nasdaq-listed company also authorized a $20 million share repurchase program.

articles.title: Hunter Biden’s $LAPTOP coin causes ‘bloodbath’ for investors. How to protect yourself
articles.summary: Over 15,000 investors suffered major losses, some within minutes.
articles.body:
Moneywise and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue through links in the content below.

Over 600,000 new cryptocurrencies were created in just the first days of 2026, according to Binance (1), a digital asset marketplace and crypto exchange. A surprising number of them have come from people in the political realm, including President Trump's $TRUMP coin (2) and the first lady's $MELANIA coin, which was created as part of the Melania Meme (3) project.

Now, a big name from the left side of the aisle has decided to get in on the action. On Sept. 9, Hunter Biden launched his own meme coin (4), $LAPTOP, named for some of the most controversial coverage of the younger Biden during Joe Biden's presidential run.

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

A record 45% of central banks plan to grow gold reserves — and many investors are following suit. Get your free gold IRA guide from Priority Gold

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

The laptop story took off in 2019, when the owner of a repair shop claimed Hunter Biden had abandoned a damaged laptop. The shop owner said the laptop had compromising personal photos and emails describing foreign business deals.

It sparked a firestorm when news media were accused of suppressing details in the lead-up to the election (5).

Fast-forward, and Hunter Biden is using the famous laptop story as a springboard to launch his own crypto coin, having announced its debut early in the week of Sept. 7, with plans to issue a billion tokens.

The tokens were slated to be distributed to the coin's founders, who would receive 30%, as well as to Biden's Substack subscribers and crypto wallet owners who suffered losses on $TRUMP. Subscribers to an Andrew Callaghan-associated mailing list were also eligible.

$LAPTOP tokens issued to the founders were set to be unsellable for six months and to vest over two full years. The plan was to burn some tokens based on criteria like Democrats winning elections, $LAPTOP's price overtaking $TRUMP's price, or Bitcoin reaching an all-time high (6).

Things didn't go as planned. The token's value plummeted within minutes, falling from a peak of $190 per token to less than $2. Unsurprisingly, investors lost big, with blockchain analytics platform Bubblemaps reporting that 80% of investors who had purchased $LAPTOP lost money (7).

articles.title: Visa Positions Itself for the Next Wave of Stablecoin Payments
articles.summary: Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) is expanding its data offering to blockchain-based lenders as demand for stablecoin-linked cards accelerates. Visa said it is combining it...
articles.body:
Visa Inc. (NYSE: V ) is expanding its data offering to blockchain-based lenders as demand for stablecoin-linked cards accelerates. Visa said it is combining its VisaNet settlement data with onchain lending infrastructure to help stablecoin card programs and fintechs obtain working capital more efficiently. The company currently has more than 160 stablecoin-linked card programs, with payment volume on those programs up nearly 200% year over year, while stablecoin settlement volume has surpassed a $20 billion annualized run rate, more than 15 times the level a year earlier.

The initiative addresses a practical constraint for fast-growing stablecoin card issuers: they need capital to fund daily settlement obligations before collecting money from cardholders. Visa Inc. (NYSE:V)'s model gives blockchain lenders access to settlement-performance data, potentially allowing them to assess credit risk and provide financing faster. Visa has already been piloting the approach with Credit Coop, with more than $2.5 billion in cumulative financed settlement volume since 2023 across participating facilities and no reported defaults.

Stablecoins Could Become a New Growth Engine

The biggest bullish takeaway is that Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) is positioning itself to capture more payment activity without having to replace its existing card network. The rapid expansion of stablecoin-linked cards suggests that crypto-native payment products are increasingly using Visa's infrastructure to reach traditional merchants. With more than 160 programs already live and payment volume growing nearly 200% year over year, continued adoption could create an incremental source of transaction volume for Visa.

Visa is also going beyond simply allowing stablecoins to run over its network. By connecting VisaNet settlement data with onchain lending, the company is helping solve the financing problem that could otherwise slow the growth of these programs. If easier access to working capital allows smaller fintechs and stablecoin issuers to launch and scale cards faster, Visa could benefit from a network-effect cycle: more issuers → more cards → more transactions → more settlement volume. Its broader partnership with Bridge, which is targeting expansion of stablecoin-linked Visa cards to more than 100 countries, further supports the potential for global adoption.

There is also a strategic benefit. Stablecoins could represent a significant evolution in payments, and Visa appears to be positioning itself as an infrastructure layer between traditional commerce and blockchain finance rather than treating crypto as a threat. Reuters notes that recent U.S. regulation has provided greater legitimacy and clarity for payment stablecoins, although important regulatory questions remain. If stablecoins become increasingly mainstream, Visa's early investment in the ecosystem could strengthen its long-term competitive position.

articles.title: 172-year-old bank sees 400% upside for 'federal bank' token
articles.summary: Analyst at a 172-year-old bank reveals a wild price target for a digital token.
articles.body:
Sky Protocol, earlier known as MakerDAO , is a decentralized finance (DeFi) project built on Ethereum .

The crypto project is best known for its USDS stablecoin. Pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar, USDS attempts to keep its value the same as that of the dollar.

As per the onchain analytics platform DeFiLlama , USDS has a market cap of more than $6 billion and accounts for over 2% of the total stablecoin market.

Sky Protocol's governance token, SKY, gives holders the right to vote on the protocol's future. With a market cap of $1.38 billion, SKY is the 62nd largest cryptocurrency.

Standard Chartered analyst says SKY will outperform Bitcoin through 2028

On Sep. 11, Standard Chartered initiated coverage of the SKY token with a price target of $0.325 by the end of 2028.

The 172-year-old bank's global head of digital assets research, Geoff Kendrick, compared the Sky Protocol to a "federal bank" as the crypto project issues stablecoins, has a governance framework, and lends assets at a wholesale interest rate. In fact, Sky is also the largest issuer of yield-bearing stablecoins.

Sky lets users stake the USDS stablecoin in exchange for the sUSDS token. Not only does the user earn the staking rewards on their USDS holding, they can also deploy the sUSDS token across the DeFi ecosystem.

As per DeFiLlama , sUSDS has a total value locked of $4.59 billion and offers an annual percentage yield (APY) of 3.6%.

The SKY token holders primarily rely on staking rewards for returns, though token buybacks also generate returns, Kendrick said.

Kendrick mentioned $0.065 as SKY's current price. It means his 2028 target of $0.325 represents an upside of 400%.

Standard Chartered sees Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH) hitting $300,000 and $18,000 by the end of 2028.

As per the analyst, the latest prediction implies that SKY will keep pace with Ether but outperform Bitcoin through 2028.

articles.summary: Three crypto ETFs each reversed course on the same day, but they reversed in three completely different directions, and only one of those reversals carries e...
articles.body:
Ethereum ETFs pulled in $216 million on September 11 while Bitcoin ETFs bled outflows for a fourth straight day, losing $13 million.

Bitcoin's swing from a $987 million inflow week to four consecutive outflow days marks the sharpest reversal to watch across crypto ETFs.

XRP ETFs traded $36 million on Friday without creating or redeeming a single share, exposing immature fund infrastructure rather than weak demand.

US spot Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) ETFs took in $216 million on Friday, September 11, 2026, while US spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) ETFs recorded a $13.29 million net outflow on their fourth straight outflow day. US spot XRP (CRYPTO:XRP) ETFs closed the session at $0.00 in net flows, per SoSoValue.

Each of the three reversed something it had been doing the week before, and they reversed in three different directions. So which of them says the most about where money is moving in crypto?

Ethereum's $216 Million Reversed a $24 Million Outflow

A net flow is what remains after subtracting the day's redemptions from the day's creations, and a creation happens when an authorized participant hands the fund cash or the underlying coin and receives new shares in return. Trading between two investors doesn't touch it.

Ethereum's $216 million follows a $24 million outflow on September 9, so the category swung from redemptions to fresh buying inside a single week. Ether traded up 3% on the day, which puts spot demand and ETF demand on the same side going into the weekend.

articles.title: Can XRP Flip Bitcoin?
articles.summary: Ripple's CTO Emeritus went on record saying XRP will surpass Bitcoin in market value, but the math behind that claim reveals just how steep the climb actuall...
articles.body:
Schwartz said XRP could surpass Bitcoin in market value, but only by growing faster on its own rather than from Bitcoin losing ground.

Reaching Bitcoin's current market cap would require XRP to hit roughly $25, more than 6 times its all-time high of $3.84.

XRP gained 35% last month against Bitcoin's 22%, which is the right direction but far short of closing a $1.49 trillion gap.

Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz said on an X Spaces on September 9 that he expects XRP (CRYPTO:XRP) to eventually pass Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) in market value, and he attached a condition to it. XRP trades at $1.36 and Bitcoin near $77,310 as of September 12.

Bitcoin's market capitalization runs between $1.54 trillion and $1.58 trillion, XRP's between $85 billion and $89 billion, a difference of about $1.49 trillion. So can XRP flip Bitcoin?

Schwartz Attached One Condition to His Answer

On the X Spaces hosted by ILLY, a listener named Angie asked Schwartz whether XRP could flip Bitcoin. His answer was "Yeah, I do." Schwartz is Ripple's CTO Emeritus and an architect of the XRP Ledger, the settlement network that clears XRP transactions and issues the coin.

"It wouldn't happen from Bitcoin shrinking. It would happen from XRP growing faster than Bitcoin," he said. Schwartz described a crypto market that keeps expanding, with XRP compounding faster inside it, so both assets rise and XRP rises more.

"I think XRP surging is probably more likely than not," he said in the same conversation. Schwartz named no price, no timeline, and no level XRP would need to clear on the way, which makes the answer an opinion about direction rather than a number anyone can trade against.
